chunks: Allah's mercy be upon Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi narrated to us, from Musa ibn 'Imran, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid, from Zayd ibn al-Mu'ddil al-Namiri and 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Verily, there is knowledge known to Allah alone, and verily there is knowledge which is known to His Closest Angels and Messengers. We also know it.

key_terms.لَا يَعْلَمُهُ غَيْرُهُ: known to none other than Him

ai.seo_question: What are the different levels of divine knowledge according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* establishes the epistemological hierarchy of divine knowledge, distinguishing between Allah’s absolute, exclusive knowledge and the derived knowledge of the Prophets and Angels. It uniquely elevates the Imams (Ahl al-Bayt) to a tier where they possess the same knowledge as the angels and prophets, a key tenet in Shia theology affirming their infallible authority and role as inheritors of the Prophet’s wisdom.
